transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I’m convinced I’ve made some terrible mistake in the books and that people are secretly watching everything I do, even though everyone keeps telling me it’s fine. My husband and my manager actually persuaded me to come in after I broke down in a meeting because I just can't trust my own judgment anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way, and did these beliefs start suddenly over days or weeks, or have they been present for months or longer?

It’s been about seven months now, starting after I took on a massive audit and began cramming for my CPA exams. It wasn't a sudden change, but more of a gradual build-up over those months. Now, this heavy feeling and the belief that I've ruined everything have been hanging over me almost nonstop.

Have you noticed any changes in your thinking, speech, emotions, or daily functioning besides this fear—for example, feeling emotionally flat, becoming more withdrawn, or having trouble organizing your thoughts?

Yes, I feel a constant, heavy emptiness and have completely withdrawn from friends and my hobby of hiking. Everything feels like it's in slow motion, making it incredibly hard to organize my thoughts in meetings or keep up with work. I've fallen so far behind that my husband has had to take over almost all of our household chores.

Over the past several months, have you also been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day, with loss of interest or pleasure, changes in sleep or appetite, low energy, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Yes, I wake up with a heavy dread in my chest every day, I've lost my appetite and dropped weight, and I feel constantly bone-tired no matter how much I sleep. I've lost all interest in my hobbies like hiking and photography because everything just feels pointless and exhausting, though I haven't actually thought about ending my life.
During this depressed period, have you ever heard voices, seen things others could not, or felt that your thoughts were being controlled or broadcast to others?

Yes, when I'm alone at my desk or trying to sleep, I hear a low, critical voice muttering that I've "cooked the books" and "ruined people's lives." I also feel certain that my clients and the firm are secretly monitoring my every move, though I don't feel like anyone is controlling or broadcasting my thoughts.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression with hallucinations or strong false beliefs before this one, or is this the first time it has ever happened?

No, this is the very first time I've ever experienced anything like this. Before this deep depression and stress started, I had never heard any accusing voices or believed that people were secretly monitoring me.
Have you ever had a previous episode like this before, with depression and hallucinations or strong false beliefs, or is this the first time it has ever happened?

No, this is completely new to me. Before all of this started about nine months ago when my workload piled up, I had never experienced this kind of heavy depression, heard any voices, or felt like I was being watched. I've always been able to handle my stress and work normally until now.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression with hallucinations or strong false beliefs before this one, or is this the first time it has ever happened?

Like I said, this is the very first time I've ever experienced anything like this. Before the stress of the CPA exams and the audit work piled up, I never had this heavy depression, heard any voices, or believed people were monitoring me. It is completely new to me.

Have you ever had a past episode of depression that lasted at least two weeks, even without hallucinations or strong false beliefs? This helps me tell whether this is the first episode or a recurrence.
No, I have never experienced an episode of depression or anything similar in the past. This is the very first time I have ever felt this way.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. I just feel completely exhausted and overwhelmed by how heavy everything is right now.

inference_history.note: Previously the candidates were [F22.0, F20.0], but the history now shows a prominent sustained depressive syndrome for about seven months: pervasive low mood/emptiness, marked withdrawal, slowed thinking, impaired functioning, and guilt/worthlessness centered on having ruined things. That makes a mood disorder with psychotic features more likely than a primary schizophrenia-spectrum illness. F20.0 is less likely because there is no clear evidence of enduring core schizophrenia features such as prominent disorganization, bizarre delusions, or characteristic negative symptoms predating the mood syndrome. F22.0 remains possible because the belief about being watched and having made a terrible mistake could still represent a persistent non-bizarre delusional system, but the depressive picture is now stronger, so the differential shifts toward a depressive episode with psychotic symptoms plus persistent delusional disorder as the main alternative.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a first lifetime episode of severe depressive symptoms lasting about 7 months, with marked anhedonia, low energy, appetite/weight loss, psychomotor/cognitive slowing, and significant functional impairment. During the depressive episode she also has mood-congruent psychotic symptoms: accusatory auditory hallucinations and persecutory/nihilistic delusional beliefs about ruining everything and being monitored. No prior manic or depressive episodes were reported.
